subject: change_brief

findings.detail: R5 targets "tests/contracts/*.test.ts" (a glob) while nfr.json (NFR1/NFR4/NFR6 verified_by) and success_criteria SC5 both point at the single existing file tests/contracts/calculator.test.ts. The glob still covers the intended file so this is not a scope or coverage defect, but tightening R5 to name the file explicitly (as the rest of the Brief/NFR already do) would remove a needless degree of freedom for solidsdd-decompose/implement.

X6 ("No change to the POST /calculate response JSON shape") is a named out-of-scope/constraint item, but no success_criteria entry directly verifies that the response shape for pow matches the existing shape (SC4 only checks that calculate() returns a ** b, not that the response envelope is unchanged). This is not a checkability hole today because the Brief's own open_questions explicitly and correctly defers exact response-shape confirmation to OpenAPI apply time with rationale (matching Change Context §7) — but decompose/judge should be aware there is currently no SC tied to X6 and may want to add one once the shape is confirmed.

All four constraints restate points already made in in_scope/out_of_scope (or nfr.json) almost verbatim (e.g. the no-precondition constraint duplicates X4/R2, the additive-enum constraint duplicates R1/NFR5). Harmless redundancy/polish, not a contradiction — every restatement is consistent with the source item it echoes.

summary: Adversarial pass. Deterministic solidsdd-lint.sh ran clean (result: pass, zero findings) — schema shape, change_id match, and id well-formedness are already verified mechanically. LLM adequacy review against change-context.md / nfr.json / change-context-gate.json found no scope-creep or scope-gap: every in_scope item (R1-R5) maps onto a specific NFR or §3 functional-intent line (R1->NFR5, R2->NFR1/NFR6, R3->NFR1's Gherkin measurement, R4->§3, R5->NFR1/NFR4/NFR6), and no NFR or §3 requirement is left without a covering in_scope item. out_of_scope correctly and explicitly excludes a precondition for pow (X4 names the exact div/mod pattern it must not inherit — b<=0, a==0, negative base with fractional exponent — matching Change Context §6's explicit anti-generalization warning almost word for word), plus memory ops, other-op behavior, new routes, response-shape changes, and overflow/special-value tightening (X1-X3, X5-X6); none of these contradict in_scope, and none of Change Context's explicit non-goals are left unlisted. success_criteria (SC1-SC6) are all concrete and independently checkable (tool commands, file contents, or test assertions named directly: Redocly lint + additive diff, OCL text inspection, Gherkin Scenario presence, switch-arm behavior, passing/negative contract-test assertions, and a no-regression check on the pre-existing suite) — none are slogan-only. human_gate.required:false was independently re-derived against the major-table triggers (material agent_default tech, stack conflict, new security/money NFR, blocking §7 item): NFR2/NFR3 are explicitly out_of_scope with rationale, the two agent_default rows in Change Context §5 (native ** operator, no formal methods) are non-material given the fixed stack and absence of a concurrency/precision signal (already independently assessed as non-gating in critique-change-context.json for the same artifact), and both §7 open_questions are marked non-blocking with precedent — so the false gate stands, matching upstream confidence:high. No blocker or major findings; three minor polish/consistency notes listed above do not affect checkability and do not change the result.
